value.author: samMularczyk
value.layerInfo: Repeating marks keyed off luminance: hatching, engraving, cross stitch, lines, rings, spiral or squares.

pattern: Which mark to draw. The first three are threshold-layered; the rest are continuous-width lines.
size: Line period, or cell size for Cross Stitch, in pixels.
lineWidth: Thickness of the marks. Interacts with Size: the ratio of the two sets how solid dark areas go.
angle: Direction of the Lines pattern, in degrees. Unused by the other patterns.
softness: Edge softness of the continuous line patterns, in period units. Small values give crisp lines.
threshold1: Crosshatch only. Luminance below which the first family appears. Luminance here is length(RGB), so the range is 0 to 1.74.
threshold2: Crosshatch only. Luminance below which the second, crossing family appears.
threshold3: Crosshatch only. Luminance below which the third family appears.
threshold4: Crosshatch only. The darkest areas get all four families.
offset: Crosshatch only. Shifts the third and fourth families so they do not sit on top of the first two.
warpAmount: Currency only. How far the lines wander, as a fraction of the layer height.
warpFrequency: Currency only. Wave cycles across the layer height.
layers: Currency only. How many of the six line families to draw. Fewer gives a sparser pattern.
brightness: Cross Stitch only. Gain on the thread colour; the original used 1.4 to stop stitches reading too dark.
invert: Cross Stitch only. Swap thread and background, so stitches become solid ink and the gaps carry the image.
inkColor: Colour of the mark. Cross Stitch takes its thread colour from the image instead, unless Invert Stitch is on.
transparentPaper: Output the mark and its alpha only, with no background, so it composites straight over whatever sits behind the layer.
amount: Mix between the original layer and the hatched result.
